title: Fear and greed in your own head
desc: Spot the two feelings that cut winners short and let losers run

cards.title: Winning most trades
cards.situation: You close winners fast at +$50, scared the gain will vanish. You hold losers to −$150, hoping they come back. You win 6 of 10 trades. Are you making money?

visual.title: Your last 10 trades
visual.label: Six wins of +$50 and four losses of −$150

options.text: Yes: you win most of your trades
options.feedback: Easy to miss: winning often isn’t the same as making money. The few losses are three times the size of the wins.
Small wins and big losses. Fear cut the winners short and hope let the losers run.
Add it up: the four losses are bigger than the six wins put together. Each loss is three times the size of a win.

cards.title: Two feelings in every trade
cards.text: Every trader feels **[[fear-and-greed|fear]]** and **[[fear-and-greed|greed]]**. They aren’t the problem. Letting them make the decisions is.

items.label: A dial from fear through calm to greed, pointing at calm

items.text: Skips good setups after a loss.
Trades too big. Holds past the target.

cards.title: The cycle every market repeats
cards.text: Fear and greed move the whole crowd in this loop. When it feels safest, risk is often highest.

visual.label: The market emotion cycle, from hope to euphoria, then down through fear and panic to despair

blocks.tip: A classic picture, not a timing tool.

cards.title: Where the money leaks
cards.text: Two of your trades. Both had a plan: stop at −$50, target at +$300.

items.title: Winner · closed by fear
items.label: The winner was sold at +$50, then went on to the +$300 target

items.title: Loser · held on hope
items.label: The loser passed the −$50 stop and was held to −$150

blocks.tip: The fix: set the stop and the target before you enter. Then let the plan decide, not the feeling.

cards.title: Name the feeling
cards.q: You’re up $80 on a trade with a $200 target. Nothing on the chart has changed, but you want to close now, “before it’s gone”. Which feeling is that?

visual.title: Open trade
visual.label: An open trade at +$80, with the target at +$200

options.feedback: Easy to mix up. Greed wants more. The urge to grab a small gain before it disappears is fear of losing it.
Nothing on the chart changed. Only the feeling did: the worry that the gain will vanish.
Boredom makes you trade when nothing is happening. Here you want out of a winner before the gain disappears.
Confidence would let the trade run to the $200 target. Grabbing $80 “before it’s gone” comes from worry.

cards.title: Best defense
cards.q: What’s the best defense against fear and greed?

options.text: Trust your gut on each trade
options.feedback: Most people go with their gut, but that’s where fear and greed live. A plan made before the trade, while you’re calm, decides for you.

options.text: Set entry, stop and target before you trade
options.feedback: A plan made while you’re calm decides the trade, so fear and greed don’t get a vote.
Watching every tick feeds the feelings. Each wiggle pulls you toward closing early or holding too long.

options.text: Trade bigger so each win counts
options.feedback: Bigger size makes every move feel bigger, so fear and greed get louder, not quieter.

cards.headline: You can spot fear and greed in your trades.
lines: Fear closes winners early. Hope lets losers run.
Winning often isn’t the same as making money.
Set stop and target before you enter, then follow them.
